title: Consent to contact-sport contacts
signal: Player is injured during a contact sport by a customary, in-bounds contact.
student_move: Cut the injury-defeats-consent myth and the absolute 'never' overclaim; in a CLASH of two 'yes' answers, pick the one that names consent to scope-of-play contacts.
tiny_rule: A participant in a contact sport impliedly consents to bodily contacts that are customary and within the ordinary rules of the game.
trap: The absolute 'never covers intentional contact' sounds like a clean rule.

title: Republication and attribution
signal: An editor or host republishes a defamatory accusation to a wider audience under attribution to the original source.
student_move: Cut the medium-based and joinder defenses on the answer text. Then use the Gold Key to kill the attribution-as-defense trap.
tiny_rule: Attribution is not a defense to republication; the republisher is on the hook for the defamatory sting.
trap: Saying 'a caller said' or 'a parent said' feels protective; it does not insulate the republisher.

title: Consent to medical contact — revocation before contact
signal: A patient signs a consent form, then clearly revokes consent before the contact. The doctor proceeds anyway. Battery suit follows.
student_move: Cut minor-injection with the Silver Key; cut written-consent-cannot-be-withdrawn with the Gold Key; cut consent-never-a-defense with the foundational rule.
tiny_rule: A signed consent is a present license; the patient can revoke it at any time before the contact.
trap: The signed form looks like a contract; consent is not a contract — it is a present license.

title: Traditional entrant categories — unknown trespasser / natural condition
signal: An entrant ignores posted no-entry signs, crosses onto a remote parcel, and is injured by a naturally fallen branch on an unmaintained footpath. The landowner did not know of the entrant.
student_move: Cut full-invitee-inspection-duty and warn-every-natural-condition with the Gold Key; cut strict-liability with the Silver Key.
tiny_rule: Unknown trespasser + natural condition on remote land = limited duty.
trap: The student fuses any on-land injury with the highest duty; the categories track the owner's invitation and the hazard type.

title: Concealment plus misstatement is fraud
signal: A seller knew of a material defect, covered it up, and made an affirmative misstatement to a buyer who relied and suffered damages.
student_move: Cut the overclaim (every defect is fraud), the wrong-element economic-loss bar, and the mislabel that fraud can never be concealment. The fraud elements are satisfied.
tiny_rule: Active concealment plus an affirmative misstatement is actionable fraud.
trap: The overclaim that every property defect is fraud is the dominant trap; the mislabel that fraud can never be concealment is the second trap.

title: Chattel retrieval — qualified privilege + damages measure
signal: A chattel lands on a landowner's land through no fault of the actor; the actor enters to retrieve; damage from entry; hauling not abnormally dangerous.
student_move: Cut under-compensation and full-privilege misreads. Apply the Gold Key: spill-caused damage is not recoverable; removal-caused damage is.
tiny_rule: Qualified privilege protects the entry, not the damage the entry itself causes.
trap: Treating the spill as the entry-caused event and stacking all downstream damage onto the actor (the spill-causation overreach).

title: Prospective advantage vs. competition privilege
signal: No signed renewal; competitor quotes a truthful lower price; long-time supplier sues the competitor.
student_move: Cut the 'any lost deal' and 'privilege only for existing contracts' answers on visible defects; the privilege answer is residual.
tiny_rule: Truthful price competition is privileged competition for prospective business; improper means are required for liability.
trap: Long-time relationship feels protective, but the privilege is the deciding line on these facts.

title: Malicious prosecution — favorable-termination threshold
signal: A plaintiff sues for malicious prosecution while the underlying proceeding is still pending, even though malice and lack of probable cause are alleged.
student_move: Apply the threshold check: has the prior proceeding terminated in a manner affirming the plaintiff's innocence of the charge or wrong? If not, the claim is not available.
tiny_rule: Favorable termination is a threshold element; a pending underlying suit is fatal to malicious prosecution.
trap: Spite or lack of probable cause is a strong showing on one element, but it cannot substitute for a missing element on another.

title: Invitee vs licensee duty — invitees get the inspection duty
signal: Possessor invites the public onto the premises for a paid event; entrant is injured; call asks what duty the possessor owed.
student_move: Classify the entrant first. If the entrant paid admission (or otherwise entered for a purpose that benefits the possessor) → invitee → reasonable care including inspection. If the entrant entered for the entrant's own purpose with permission → licensee → warn only of known hazards.
tiny_rule: Invitees get the inspection duty; the 'warn only of known' rule is the licensee standard.
trap: The dominant trap is the invitee-vs-licensee conflation. Many students half-remember that 'landowners only have to warn' and pick the narrower licensee rule for paying invitees.

title: Open and obvious danger — failure to warn does not arise
signal: An ordinary product, an ordinary-use risk, and a plaintiff sues for failure to warn of that exact risk.
student_move: Cut the consequence-instead-of-cause and the categorical-exclusion distractors first. Then apply the Gold Key: open-and-obvious risks never trigger the duty to warn.
tiny_rule: Open and obvious = no duty to warn.
trap: The dominant trap is the 'every dangerous product needs a warning' claim (tiered absolute). It is engineered to look like the safe default; the doctrine carves out the obvious risks.

title: Joint and several liability — plaintiff collects 100% from any one defendant; contribution is inter-se
signal: Multiple defendants held jointly and severally liable; plaintiff free of fault; call asks what portion the plaintiff may collect from one defendant.
student_move: Distinguish the plaintiff's collection right from the defendants' inter-se contribution problem. The plaintiff may collect 100% from any one defendant; the defendants' inter-se contribution claim is a separate question.
tiny_rule: Joint and several = plaintiff collects 100% from any one defendant; the proportional split is the defendants' inter-se problem, not the plaintiff's.
trap: The dominant trap is the proportional-liability / contribution confusion. Many students half-remember that 'multiple defendants means a proportional split' and apply the defendants' inter-se rule to the plaintiff's collection right.

title: Res ipsa and the third-prong plaintiff-contribution test
signal: The plaintiff has materially altered the instrumentality after leaving the defendant's control, and the cause of the accident is undetermined between the defendant's defect and the plaintiff's alteration.
student_move: Apply the third prong of the res ipsa test: a post-rental plaintiff alteration is a plausible alternative cause wholly attributable to the plaintiff, and the inference collapses.
tiny_rule: Res ipsa is unavailable when the plaintiff's own post-receipt conduct is a plausible alternative cause.
trap: The 'never unless the maker was negligent' wording is the dominant trap; carved wooden items can and do fail when a renter drills into the structural base.

title: Assault — plaintiff-side apprehension and the transferred-intent scope
signal: A bystander (the plaintiff) sues an attacker for assault over harm the attacker directed at a third party; the attacker never threatened the bystander.
student_move: Apply the assault elements: the plaintiff must apprehend imminent contact with HERSELF. The transferred-intent doctrine does not supply a missing plaintiff-side apprehension.
tiny_rule: Transferred intent does not apply to assault.
trap: The transferred-intent doctrine is a real doctrine; the trap is the doctrinal misapplication, not the doctrine's existence. Also: 'awareness of fright' is not 'apprehension of contact with self.'

title: Coming to the nuisance is a factor, not a defense
signal: Defendant argues 'coming to the nuisance' after a substantial expansion of the activity following the plaintiff's move-in.
student_move: Cut the complete-defense overclaim. The doctrine is a reasonableness factor, not a complete defense. An *expansion* after the plaintiff's arrival cuts strongly against the 'was there first' intuition.
tiny_rule: Coming to the nuisance is a factor, not a complete defense; an expansion of the activity after the plaintiff moved in makes the doctrine weakest.
trap: The 'was there first' intuition pulls toward the complete-defense overclaim.

title: Appropriation and scope of consent
signal: A person licenses a photo for a limited use, and the licensee later uses the photo for a different medium and a later time period.
student_move: Compare the original license's scope to the later use on each scope dimension (time, medium, purpose). If any dimension is exceeded, the use is unauthorized and the appropriation claim survives.
tiny_rule: A license to use a likeness is limited by its scope; use outside the agreed scope can support an appropriation claim.
trap: The 'once-consented-always-consented' intuition pulls toward 'permanent and unlimited.' The 'flattering photo' intuition is irrelevant. The 'false fact' theory belongs to a different privacy tort.

title: AS-IS / obvious writing kills justifiable reliance
signal: Oral assurance + signed contradictory writing in obvious form (bold type, above signature)
student_move: Spot the visible writing. Cut all 'fraud applies' / 'reliance presumed' overclaim distractors. Lock the 'justifiable reliance defeated by obvious writing' answer.
tiny_rule: Justifiable reliance requires the reliance to be reasonable in light of plainly visible contradictory information the plaintiff signed.
trap: The contract-integration misframe (parol evidence lane) and the broad-absolute 'fraud never applies' overclaim.

title: Lost wages are parasitic damages when they flow from a tort-caused physical injury
signal: Negligence claim, plaintiff has a physical injury, plaintiff seeks lost wages or lost self-employed contract income, defendant invokes 'pure economic loss.'
student_move: Cut the 'all financial loss is pure economic loss' overclaim, the nominal-only remedy, and the contract-theory frame. Apply the Gold Key: financial harm that flows from a tort-caused physical injury is recoverable parasitic damages.
tiny_rule: Lost wages are parasitic on a tort-caused physical injury; the standalone pure economic loss bar does not apply when the plaintiff has a physical injury.
trap: The dominant trap is treating 'pure economic loss' as an absolute bar to financial recovery in negligence. The bar is a no-physical-injury bar; once a physical injury is present, the financial harm rides in on the personal-injury claim.

title: Fraud requires justifiable reliance; reliance is defeated by ignoring an obvious contradiction
signal: Fraud suit, pre-sale written document plainly contradicts the oral assurance, plaintiff did not read the document.
student_move: Cut the private-law contract trope (oral overrides written), the no-reliance-element misstatement, and the fact/opinion confusion. Apply the Gold Key: ignoring an obvious, plainly-worded contradiction can defeat justifiable reliance as a matter of law.
tiny_rule: Justifiable reliance is a flexible reasonableness standard; reliance on an obvious written contradiction of an oral assurance is not justified.
trap: The dominant trap is the fact/opinion confusion: the student treats a verifiable historical fact (page replacement) as if it were a value judgment or connoisseur's opinion. The other strong trap is the private-law contract trope (oral overrides written).

title: Defamation requires falsity; substantial truth tolerates minor inaccuracies
signal: A private publication misstates a date (month) of an otherwise-true defamatory fact (license revocation, criminal charge, professional sanction, etc.); the plaintiff sues based only on the wrong date. The call is the best defense.
student_move: Identify the defamatory sting. If the sting is true — even if a minor detail (month, day, year) is wrong — substantial truth is the defense. The 'any mistake defeats truth' framing is the any-inaccuracy myth.
tiny_rule: A statement is not defamatory if the gist or sting is substantially true, even if minor details are inaccurate.
trap: The any-inaccuracy myth is the dominant trap. Many students half-remember that 'defamation requires truth' and reason that any mistake (even a one-month error) makes the statement false.

title: Warned risk is not warning defect
signal: The answer says the plaintiff suffered the exact risk described.
student_move: Ask whether the call is about injury or about warning duty.
tiny_rule: Injury completes harm; it does not prove the warning was defective.
trap: Wrong-element answer on failure-to-warn claims.

title: Control Beats Title
signal: Non-owner had authority over who could use the chattel.
student_move: Ask who supplied or permitted use, then ask whether the user was visibly unsafe.
tiny_rule: For negligent entrustment, supplier/control can be enough; title is not the gate.
trap: Owner-only answer.

title: Foreseeability is not the whole duty gate.
signal: Professional information + economic loss + unknown later reader.
student_move: Ask: targeted person/class and targeted transaction?
tiny_rule: Foreseeability alone loses to targeted-use duty.
trap: General negligence reflex.

title: False-light public concern: fault before feelings
signal: False-light claim plus public-concern publication.
student_move: Lock the call. If it asks mental state, find the publisher's knowledge or serious doubt.
tiny_rule: Actual malice is knowledge of falsity or reckless disregard.
trap: Mistaking embarrassment, special damages, or misleading graphics for the required mental-state showing.

title: Later Fix Is Not Hindsight Liability
signal: Post-injury repair, added guard, new warning, new traction, or changed procedure.
student_move: Separate prior breach from later feasibility.
tiny_rule: Later fix is not breach proof; feasibility only if genuinely disputed.
trap: They fixed it later, so they must have breached earlier.

title: Res ipsa: inference, not proof shortcut to judgment
signal: Abnormal malfunction, defendant responsibility, plaintiff non-contribution, no direct proof.
student_move: Do not punish the plaintiff for lacking the exact defect; ask whether the event itself can speak.
tiny_rule: No exact defect needed; no automatic judgment.
trap: Missing direct proof feels fatal.

title: Cause/status/product are not the claim
signal: A Torts answer names only cause, status, or product defect.
student_move: Ask whether the answer supplies a liability basis.
tiny_rule: For negligence, look for unreasonable conduct.
trap: Choosing a legally flavored fragment instead of the operative ground.

title: Who paid?
signal: Insurance payment before or after tort verdict.
student_move: Sort the payer: defendant-side, joint-tortfeasor-side, or plaintiff-side.
tiny_rule: Plaintiff-side insurance does not reduce the judgment.
trap: Double recovery feels fair but points the wrong way.

title: Owner-inspection fact beats product/contractor/status bait
signal: Premises owner is sued after a third party installed a dangerous device.
student_move: Ask which choice supplies breach by the named owner.
tiny_rule: For invitees, reasonable inspection can be the breach path.
trap: Product defect and contractor conduct feel causal but do not answer owner breach.

title: Danger invites rescue, not automatic indemnity
signal: Rescuer injured while responding to apparent human peril.
student_move: Ask whether the defendant's unreasonable conduct created the danger; then reject actual-awareness and automatic-payment traps.
tiny_rule: Rescue is foreseeable when negligent danger creates apparent human peril.
trap: Treating rescue as either meddling or automatic reimbursement.

title: Name/photo trap in appropriation
signal: The stem says no exact name or photograph, but many identity cues are copied.
student_move: Do not require exact name/photo. Ask whether the ad clearly uses the plaintiff’s identity for commercial advantage without consent.
tiny_rule: Recognizable commercial evocation can be enough.
trap: Exact-name/photo-only answer.

title: Rescue Doctrine: Actor-Fault Gate
signal: Rescuer is hurt and sues the person rescued or that person's estate.
student_move: Target the defendant's negligence before praising the rescue.
tiny_rule: No negligent peril-maker, no rescuer recovery from that defendant.
trap: Noble rescue facts feel dispositive.

title: False light publicity gate
signal: False-light claim after a private accusation.
student_move: Ask whether the matter reached the public or a broad audience.
tiny_rule: One private listener is not false-light publicity.
trap: Treating falsity or defamation overlap as enough.

title: Avoidability is not contributory negligence
signal: Choice says plaintiff would have avoided injury if she had acted differently.
student_move: Ask whether the choice says the actual conduct was negligent.
tiny_rule: No plaintiff negligence, no contributory-negligence bar.
trap: Confusing safer hypothetical with legal fault.

title: Breach is not causation
signal: The stem proves what the doctor should have done but not what would have happened if the doctor had done it.
student_move: Ask: what evidence links this specific missed step to this specific injury?
tiny_rule: No link, no negligence win.
trap: Choosing the answer that proves breach or the answer that proves the procedure caused harm.

title: Known recipient, not no one and not everyone
signal: Professional report prepared for a named recipient's business reliance.
student_move: Cut the extremes: no-contract is too narrow; every-foreseeable is too broad.
tiny_rule: Known recipient or limited known group can recover for careless false business information.
trap: Students choose either strict privity or unlimited foreseeability.

title: Strict Liability Needs the Risk Link
signal: Dangerous activity plus ordinary injury.
student_move: Ask what hurt the plaintiff before choosing a strict-liability answer.
tiny_rule: Activity label is not enough; injury must flow from the abnormal risk.
trap: Picking the dangerous-activity label.

title: Battery mental-state target
signal: Battery answer set offers contact, injury, risk, and motive.
student_move: Lock the call, then pick the answer that targets contact.
tiny_rule: Contact intent beats injury/risk/motive.
trap: Choosing the more serious-sounding injury or risk answer.

title: Special category beats ordinary NIED gate
signal: Stem gives a recognized emotional-distress category.
student_move: Do not import zone-of-danger or bystander requirements unless the call asks for the ordinary rule.
tiny_rule: Recognized erroneous death notice is its own NIED lane.
trap: Physical danger sounds like the default NIED screen.

title: Nuisance Remedy Oversteer
signal: The answer says total shutdown, no remedy, or punitive-only.
student_move: Ask which remedy fits the abatement fact.
tiny_rule: Tailor the fix; limit avoidable damages.
trap: All-or-nothing remedy language.

title: Foreseeability target scan
signal: All answers ask what had to be foreseeable.
student_move: Name the object after 'foreseeable that' before judging law.
tiny_rule: Pick the plaintiff/risk target, not the old cause, exact chain, or defendant breach.
trap: Students pick the most dramatic fact instead of the legal target.

title: Independent contractor is not the end of the story
signal: Hirer has a statutory/public safety duty and hires someone else to perform it.
student_move: Ask whether the duty itself can be delegated.
tiny_rule: Nondelegable duty can keep liability with the hirer.
trap: Contractor status as total shield.
